text:
alex: FYI seeing ~28 pods in Pending in us-central1-a since 08:14. All request 1gpu small-gang jobs. Scheduler keeps hopping them across AZs and leaving single-GPU holes. Anyone seen similar?
riley: Yep, I saw that spike. Logs show a flurry of Bind attempts then 'unschedulable: insufficient resources' despite node GPU util being 0.1-0.2 on several nodes.
toni: quick `kubectl describe pod` shows:
```
Events:
  08:14:05  FailedScheduling  0/60 nodes are available: 12 node(s) had taint {gpu.reserve=warm:NoSchedule}, 18 node(s) had unfulfilled topologySpreadConstraints, 30 node(s) had insufficient accelerator (requested:1, found:0).
```
kevin: Two things colliding: warm-reserve taints plus our strict topologySpread (hard) + the topology plugin trying to spread across racks for reliability. When a few nodes flapped NotReady earlier, the scheduler overcompensated and spread new pods, producing single-gpu holes.
alex: sched-bot: METRIC_ALERT packing_hole_rate_us-central1-a > 15/min for 15m
sched-bot: automated hint: consider enabling backfill_toleration for best-effort queues or reduce topologySpread to 'preferDuringScheduling' for tiny jobs.
riley: Short-term mitigation I suggest: 1) patch the low-priority WorkQueue to add toleration `gpu.reserve=warm:NoSchedule` (only for Preemptible class), 2) change topologySpreadConstraint from 'Must' to 'Prefer' for that queue, 3) enable 5m scheduler batching window to allow coalescing.
toni: I'm worried about side-effects on rack-level fault tolerance if we relax spread. Maybe do a canary in us-central1-a on 10 pods, observe eviction and p99- latency.
kevin: Agree canary. Also add a quick K8s resource check: `kubectl get nodes -o custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU_ALLOC:.status.allocatable.gpu,GPU_USED:.status.capacity.gpu` to verify real allocable values after the node NotReady repairs.
alex: I'll run the canary: patching queue -> toleration + prefer spread. Rolling to 10 pods now. Commands: `kubectl patch deployment low-priority-queue -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"tolerations":[{"key":"gpu.reserve","operator":"Equal","value":"warm","effect":"NoSchedule"}]}}}}'` and `kubectl patch deployment low-priority-queue -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"topologySpreadConstraints":[{"maxSkew":1,"topologyKey":"rack","whenUnsatisfiable":"PreferDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution"}]}}}}'`
riley: I'll watch metrics: packing_hole_rate, eviction_rate, and p99_schedule_latency. If packing_hole_rate drops >50% in 10m we keep change, otherwise roll back.
toni: Add runbook note: if eviction_rate spikes > 25/min after canary, immediately revert toleration and restore strict spread.
sched-bot: NOTE: predicted cost impact: warmer utilization +0.6% for best-effort workloads; predicted SLO improvement ~6%.
alex: Can confirm canary applied. Monitoring now. Will post updates in 10m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
